samples.summary: The replay lane's dry-run step passes `--panel-script`/`--panel-sha` but not `--panel-digest`, and `run.mjs`'s new `resolvePanelDigest` hard-refuses a non-sibling panel script without it
samples.evidence: .github/workflows/eval-replay.yml:388-391 builds `ARGS+=(--panel-script scripts/agent/eval/adapters/stub-panel.mjs --panel-sha 0000...)` for `PANEL != real`, then runs `node scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs` (line 393). The new guard in scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs `resolvePanelDigest` throws `--panel-script points at ... Pass --panel-digest` whenever `path.resolve(panelScript) !== path.resolve(DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT)` and no override is given. The dry-run leg of eval-replay.yml therefore aborts before any item is replayed. run.test.mjs was updated to pass `--panel-digest` (runCli), but the workflow was not. Fix belongs in the workflow (add `--panel-digest sha256:<64 hex>`).

samples.summary: score-all hands a digest it READ from envelopes down as `--panel-digest`, and report.mjs interprets that flag as an operator assertion, so every filed cross-run score records `panel_digest_source: "reconstructed"` for a digest that was actually observed
samples.evidence: score-all.mjs `panelFlags` (≈line 615-624) passes `--panel-digest <panel>` whenever the resolution produced a real digest, and `panel` comes from `resolvePanelDigest({records: store.panelDigestRecords(ids)})` — i.e. source `envelopes`. report.mjs's `resolvePanel` (≈line 3369-3376) treats any `--panel-digest` as stated and returns `{source: "reconstructed"}`, printing "was STATED on the command line, not read from the runs". `withPanelStamp` then writes `panel_digest_source: "reconstructed"` into the payload and `validateScorePanel` accepts it. Result: once runs actually record digests, every score filed by the standard lane misattributes its own provenance — exactly the `files`/`reconstructed` distinction store.mjs refuses decorative values for. score-all.test.mjs:693-697 reproduces the same rule in its spy (`const source = stated ? "reconstructed" : resolved?.source`), so no test can catch it.

samples.summary: `--allow-mixed-panel` is unreachable on the render path: report.mjs still refuses any pool whose runs name more than one `panel_sha`, which a mixed digest almost always implies
samples.evidence: report.mjs:3477-3481 (unchanged by this diff) exits 1 when `stated.size > 1` panel_sha values across the named runs. A mixed `panel_digest` means the panels differ by content, which in practice means they were read from different commits — so the very population the new opt-out exists for (the cited 16-item / 5-panel run) hits this refusal immediately after `resolvePanel` allowed it at line 3450. score-all.mjs then converts that exit into `refuse("report.mjs exited ...")` after the scoring budget has already been spent, which is what the new pre-flight refusal was meant to avoid. Either the panel_sha unanimity check has to admit the mixed case or `--allow-mixed-panel` cannot be exercised end to end.

samples.summary: Two cross-run scorers still key reviewer identity on `(config_hash, panel_sha)` and abort on differing shas, contradicting the new digest-based poolability and breaking a score-all pass over the data this change targets
samples.evidence: reliability.mjs `assertOneReviewer` (lines 366-405) builds identities from `config_hash` + `panel_sha` and refuses at line 393-396 when more than one is present; cost-latency.mjs:766 calls the same helper. score-all.mjs runs both as STEPS. So for the population this change is justified by — "16 item envelopes carrying 16 distinct panel_sha values, which are 5 distinct panels by content" — the digest resolution now says "one panel, poolable" while reliability-v1 and cost-latency-v1 still refuse, and the pass fails. The premise that a commit-keyed identity over-separates was not propagated to the two modules that enforce it.

samples.summary: The panel adapter normalises `config_hash`/`panel_sha` off the envelope but not `panel_digest`, so no scorer that consumes adapter records can see or enforce the new identity
samples.evidence: adapters/panel.mjs:83-85 builds the record's `panel` block as `{config_hash, panel_sha}` only. reliability.mjs:378 reads `r.panel.panel_sha` for its identity check and reliability.mjs:1314-1319 copies only `config_hash`/`panel_sha` off the envelope, so the digest recorded by this change never reaches any scorer's pooling check — the guard exists only at the store/filing door. The test fixture adapters/panel.test.mjs:31 was given a `panel_digest` but nothing reads it.
searchedFor: grep panel_sha -C4 in reliability.mjs and segmentation.mjs

samples.summary: The render path resolves the panel before it checks the named runs exist, so a typo'd run id now surfaces as "a cross-run score must name the records it pools" instead of "run does not exist"
samples.evidence: report.mjs:3450 calls `resolvePanel(runIds)` while the run-existence loop that exits 1 with a precise message is at 3464-3476. `store.panelDigestRecords` skips unknown run ids (store.mjs `panelDigestRecords`, `if (run === null) continue`), so with all ids bad the list is empty and `resolvePanelDigest` throws out of `main`, printing `report failed: panel identity: a cross-run score must name the records it pools`. The same ordering applies to score-all's own resolution, which runs before its existing per-run `getRun` check only in the pre-flight case.

samples.summary: `run.mjs` exports a second, incompatible `resolvePanelDigest` alongside `panel-identity.mjs`'s exported function of the same name
samples.evidence: run.mjs exports `resolvePanelDigest({panelScript, override, digestOf})` returning `{panelDigest, source}`, while panel-identity.mjs exports `resolvePanelDigest({records, allowMixed})` returning `{digest, mixed, tally, source}`. score-all.mjs:47 and report.mjs:79 import the panel-identity one; run.test.mjs:34 imports the run.mjs one. Today no module imports both, but two same-named exports with different parameter and return shapes in sibling modules of the same directory is an easy mis-import that no lane would catch (neither package has tsc coverage over scripts/).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `resolvePanelDigest` (scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs:580-597) throws whenever `--panel-script` resolves to something other than DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT (`scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs`, run.mjs:82) and no `--panel-digest` override is given; the only override source is the CLI flag (run.mjs:795 — no env/config fallback), and it is called unconditionally before any work at run.mjs:852-855. The caller in .github/workflows/eval-replay.yml:386-393 appends only `--panel-script scripts/agent/eval/adapters/stub-panel.mjs` and `--panel-sha 0000...` for the default `panel: stub` leg (input default at eval-replay.yml:75-79) and then invokes `node scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs` at line 393. A grep for `digest|DIGEST` over the whole workflow file returns zero matches, and line 393 is its only run.mjs invocation. I searched wide for an indirect supplier — every `--panel-script` reference repo-wide (workflow, run.mjs, run.test.mjs:269 which does pass a digest, replay-plan.mjs:91 comment, docs, and the stale `.trusted/` snapshot that the workflow never references), plus env-var/config fallbacks — and found no path that supplies `--panel-digest` to this invocation. So the dry-run leg aborts before replaying any item: a changed contract (new required flag) with an unupdated caller, in-lane and major.

verdict.reason: Confirmed exactly as described. score-all.mjs:724 resolves the panel via resolvePanelDigest (which stamps source "envelopes", panel-identity.mjs:464-477), and panelFlags at score-all.mjs:622-627 forwards any real digest as `--panel-digest` (used at :597, :606, :789, :801) with no distinction between operator-stated and envelope-read. report.mjs:3369-3377 treats the presence of `--panel-digest` as an operator assertion unconditionally, returning `source: "reconstructed"` and printing "was STATED on the command line, not read from the runs"; report.mjs:3416-3417 then passes that through withPanelStamp (report.mjs:348-353), writing panel_digest_source: "reconstructed" into the payload, and store.mjs:474-493 (validateScorePanel) only checks vocabulary membership (panel-identity.mjs:138) so it accepts it. Since the source vocabulary is explicitly non-decorative (panel-identity.mjs:114-137, store.mjs:482-492), every cross-run score filed by the standard lane misattributes its own provenance once runs record digests, and `envelopes` is unreachable through the driver. score-all.test.mjs:693-697 encodes the same rule in the spy, so no test detects it. This is a caller/contract mismatch across files (blast-radius lane), major impact: wrong provenance persisted in filed score payloads.

A mixed `panel_digest` means the panels differ by content, which in practice means they were read from different commits — so the very population the new opt-out exists for (the cited 16-item / 5-panel run) hits this refusal immediately after `resolvePanel` allowed it at line 3450. score-all.mjs then converts that exit into `refuse("report.mjs exited ...")` after the scoring budget has already been spent, which is what the new pre-flight refusal was meant to avoid. verdict.reason: The panel_sha unanimity check at report.mjs:3478-3481 builds `stated` exclusively from per-run `run.json.panel_sha` (report.mjs:3464-3477) — never from item envelopes — and `renderArgs` passes no `--panel-sha` (score-all.mjs:603-608, 622-627). The mixed-panel population the opt-out exists for is documented as a mixture WITHIN A SINGLE RUN: store.mjs:1058-1061 ("the mixture that motivated this is WITHIN a run: the live-ingested agent-PR run is one run id whose 16 item envelopes are 5 panels by content") and panel-identity.mjs:443-446 ("one ingested run pools 16 items across 5 panels by content"), with `panelDigestRecords` walking both run.json and every item envelope (store.mjs:1070-1081). For one run id, `stated.size <= 1`, so the refusal cannot fire, and the render path explicitly accepts a single run id (report.mjs:3445-3448). Additionally, `tallyPanelDigests` puts unrecorded digests in the `not-recorded` bucket (panel-identity.mjs:403-406, 421-431), so `mixed` also arises among runs naming one identical panel_sha. score-all.mjs has no panel_sha logic at all, so no second refusal exists. The claimed consequence — `--allow-mixed-panel` unreachable on the render path for the cited 16-item/5-panel run — is contradicted by that exact population, which passes the check.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described: reliability.mjs:366-406 keys reviewer identity on (config_hash, panel_sha) at lines 378/381 and hard-refuses when more than one identity is present at lines 392-397; the file contains no panel_digest handling at all (grep: no matches). cost-latency.mjs:71 imports and :766 calls the same helper, also with no digest awareness. score-all.mjs:104-105 registers reliability-v1 and cost-latency-v1 as cross-run STEPS, runs them at :766, and refuses the whole pass on any non-zero exit at :774 (reliability's CLI exits 1 on a refusal, reliability.mjs:1339-1344). The population this change is justified by is stated in the new code itself — panel-identity.mjs:19-27 and store.mjs:1054-1081 ("one run id whose 16 item envelopes are 5 panels by content", 16 distinct panel_sha) — and the diff adds an explicit poolability decision plus opt-out (panel-identity.mjs:458-478 resolvePanelDigest/allowMixed, reached from score-all.mjs:724 via --allow-mixed-panel, digest handed down only to report.mjs by panelFlags score-all.mjs:622-627). Mixed digests imply differing panel_sha, so on exactly the data the opt-out exists for, the digest layer says "poolable/file as mixed" while assertOneReviewer refuses and score-all aborts at :774 — the new capability has no working end-to-end path, and the premise that a commit-keyed identity over-separates was not propagated to the two modules that enforce it. No guard makes the refusal unreachable, and this cross-module contract mismatch outside the diff's files is squarely in the blast-radius lane, so none of not-present, already-guarded or out-of-scope applies.
